title: Check yourself: Java 8 on old code

questions.stem: A team's class `RecentIds extends AbstractList<Long> implements Set<Long>` declares get, size, add(int, Long) and remove(int). Its build moves from JDK 7 to JDK 8. What does javac do with it?

options.text: It compiles the class, and its spliterator() is List's, since the superclass AbstractList outranks the interfaces
options.says: the page's OrderedTags also extends AbstractList and is still refused, so the superclass settles nothing

options.text: It compiles the class, and its stream() is Set's, since Set is the interface the class names itself
options.says: naming an interface directly gives its defaults no priority; the conflicting defaults are List's and Set's spliterator(), so javac refuses the class

options.text: It refuses the class until it overrides spliterator(), since List and Set each bring their own default of it
options.says: List and Set each override Collection's spliterator() default; a class inheriting both must override it

options.text: It refuses the class until it overrides stream(), since List and Set each bring their own default of it
options.says: the error names spliterator(), and the fix that compiles overrides spliterator() alone

origin.section: The JDK's New Defaults Reach Classes Written Before Them, and Two of Them Can Collide

questions.stem: `SeatMap extends HashMap<String, Integer>` overrides put to throw once the map holds 100 entries. A new booking feature fills it with `seats.computeIfAbsent(seatId, id -> 0)` for 150 different seat ids. What is the map's size afterwards?

options.text: 100, and the 101st call throws, since HashMap's computeIfAbsent stores each new key by calling put
options.says: that is Map's default implementation; HashMap overrides computeIfAbsent and writes to its table without calling put

options.text: 100, and the later calls add nothing, since HashMap's computeIfAbsent skips a key whose put fails
options.says: HashMap's computeIfAbsent never calls put, so nothing fails and nothing is skipped

options.text: 150, since HashMap's computeIfAbsent stores each new key without calling put
options.says: HashMap implements the Java 8 methods itself, bypassing a subclass's put

options.text: 150, since HashMap's computeIfAbsent catches the exception from put and stores the key anyway
options.says: there is no exception to catch: HashMap's computeIfAbsent doesn't call put at all

origin.section: A Method Java 8 Added to a Collection Need Not Go Through Your Overrides

questions.stem: A library's interface `Money` declares `static Money zero()`. Your class `Euro implements Money`, and your code calls `Euro.zero()`. What does javac do?

options.text: It compiles the call to Money.zero(), since a static method is always reachable through a subtype of its declaring type
options.says: that holds for a class's static methods through a subclass, not for an interface's through an implementer

options.text: It compiles the call to a copy of zero() in Euro, since an implementing class always receives its interfaces' static methods
options.says: an implementer receives none of its interfaces' static methods, so there is nothing in Euro to call

options.text: It reports an error, since a class never inherits a static method from the interfaces it implements
options.says: interface statics belong to the interface alone; the call fails with cannot find symbol

options.text: It reports an error, since an interface's static method can be called only from code inside that interface
options.says: any code can call it on the interface name, as Money.zero(); only the call through Euro is an error

origin.section: Static Interface Methods Belong to the Interface: Implementers Don't Inherit Them

questions.stem: `Shipment implements Serializable` keeps its tracking code in a field `Optional<String> trackingCode`. The servers replicate HTTP sessions by serializing them, and a Shipment with a tracking code is stored in the session. What happens when the session is replicated?

options.text: Writing the session throws NotSerializableException, since Optional doesn't implement Serializable
options.says: Optional doesn't implement Serializable, so writing an object that holds one throws; the field compiles and works until then

options.text: Writing the session throws NotSerializableException, since a generic type like Optional<String> can't implement Serializable
options.says: generic classes can implement Serializable (ArrayList<String> does); Optional simply doesn't

options.text: The copy arrives with the tracking code intact, since Optional implements Serializable and writes its value
options.says: Optional doesn't implement Serializable, whatever it holds, so writing the object throws

options.text: The copy arrives with the tracking code empty, since Optional implements Serializable but writes no value
options.says: Optional doesn't implement Serializable, so writing the object throws before anything arrives

origin.section: An Optional Field Breaks Serialization, and an Optional Parameter Can Still Be null
